summary.overview: The static attendance app ships with no project-owned startup, validation, or contract route, so agent edits land unguarded; the session window for this review was too partial to evaluate repeated-work demand.

dimensions.label: Task Understanding
dimensions.summary: The 4-line README gives no architecture or data-boundary map, so the students.json vs Supabase split and mandatory CDN load order exist only inside code.

dimensions.label: Controlled Execution
dimensions.summary: No manifest, script, or documented startup route exists, and the admin gate is enforced client-side with a hardcoded password; the observed session sample ran edits with no supported operation or permission boundary.

dimensions.label: Change Validation
dimensions.summary: No test, lint, type, or CI mechanism is tracked, and the analyzed session sample showed 80 edit events with no later validation command; required checks are missing for every changed path.

dimensions.label: Reliable Delivery
dimensions.summary: Work is committed directly to main with near-uninformative messages and no review, CI, or release artifacts, leaving no revision-bound acceptance or bisectable recovery evidence.

dimensions.label: Learning Capture
dimensions.summary: A bounded review completed, but the session lane admitted zero episodes and the analyzer's recurrence route reported insufficient episodes and non-evaluable capture, routing, and application boundaries; no repeat or clean-window decision was possible.

findings.title: The app cannot be started reliably from a clean checkout
findings.reason: Verified project facts: 12 tracked files, no package.json, lockfile, or any script declaration, and a 4-line README with no setup or run instructions. js/config.js loads the roster with fetch('./students.json'), which fails under file:// and needs a static server, while admin.html and checkin.html mark the CDN Supabase script load order as mandatory in HTML comments only. A fresh operator or agent must guess the runtime and startup route, and a wrong guess (opening files directly) silently breaks the roster path. Analyzer lane: manifests [], entryCandidates [].
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Add the smallest startup route the project can own: a README section (or a minimal manifest with a single serve script) that names the runtime decision (a static server is required because js/config.js fetches ./students.json), the serve command, and the mandatory CDN-script load order already noted in admin.html and checkin.html comments. Do not restructure existing js/ logic.

## Validation

- From a clean shell, follow only the new instructions and confirm index.html, admin.html, and checkin.html load with the roster populated from ./students.json
- Confirm the fetch('./students.json') path works (no file:// CORS failure) using the documented route

findings.title: Code changes reach main with no check that can catch a regression
findings.reason: Verified project facts: git ls-files shows zero test, spec, lint, typecheck, or CI files (testFiles 0 in the project lane), so no material change to js/checkin.js, js/admin.js, or js/config.js can be mapped to any project-owned check; invariants asserted in commit 29d5e51 (QR expiry, XSS guard) have no mechanical regression signal. Corroborating session-window fact: the analyzer's complete 4-session census observed 80 edit events with no later validation command category. Absence is proven only for the tracked tree; external pipelines were not inspected.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Add the smallest check surface that covers the core write paths without changing app logic: either a plain-text smoke checklist in the README mapped to checkin -> attendance insert and admin -> session create, or one lightweight local check script for the pure client functions in js/config.js (for example MSSV handling and roster loading). Keep it runnable through the documented startup route only; do not assume a package manager or runtime that the repo does not already use.

## Validation

- Run the new check (or walk the checklist) once against the current tree and record the result
- Confirm the check fails when a core invariant is deliberately broken in a scratch copy
expectedOutput: Update the existing Test owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.

findings.title: The admin gate can be bypassed by viewing page source
findings.reason: Verified project facts: js/auth.js compares a hardcoded admin password literal entirely in the browser and gates admin.html with sessionStorage; js/config.js hardcodes the Supabase URL and publishable key. Any visitor can read the credential from the delivered script and reach the admin UI. Boundary kept explicit: RLS and Edge Function setup may exist server-side but was not inspectable within this review, so this finding states the present client-side exposure, not a proven data breach.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

First verify the server-side boundary before touching client code: check the Supabase project's RLS policies on the sessions and attendance tables and confirm no policy trusts the publishable key alone for admin writes. Then move the admin decision server-side using Supabase Auth (or an Edge Function) so js/auth.js no longer compares a static password in the browser. Because the current password is already published in the repository history, treat it as compromised: rotate it as part of the repair. External Supabase changes require explicit authorization before writing.

## Validation

- Confirm the admin page's protected actions fail without an authenticated server-side session
- Confirm the old client-side literal no longer authorizes any action and has been rotated
expectedOutput: Update the existing Code owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.

findings.title: A Supabase column change silently breaks app writes
findings.reason: Verified project facts: js/admin.js and js/checkin.js write to the sessions and attendance tables and subscribe to postgres_changes, but git ls-files shows no schema, migration, or contract file anywhere in the repo. The canonical definition of those tables lives outside the repository and is not comparable from within it, so a column rename or type change on the server cannot be detected by any repo mechanism before the write path fails at runtime. Distinct from the missing validation route: this is an untracked external contract, not an absent check.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Track the external contract inside the repository: add a schema file (SQL DDL or a documented column-by-column contract note) covering the sessions and attendance tables and the realtime channels the app uses, derived from what js/admin.js and js/checkin.js actually read and write. Read-only export of the current table definitions from Supabase is acceptable if authorized; do not create or alter database objects.

## Validation

- Cross-check every column referenced in js/admin.js and js/checkin.js against the new schema file and confirm no reference is undefined
- Confirm the file states which table definitions are canonical and where they are applied
expectedOutput: Update the existing Document owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.

findings.title: Commit history cannot support bisect, rollback, or acceptance
findings.reason: Verified project facts: 133 commits landed within an approximately two-day burst, all direct to main with no review or CI artifacts, and recent messages include single tokens such as "hhh", "ộ", and repeated "Update admin.html". For an agent, the practical consequence is present: a regression cannot be attributed to a change, a revert target cannot be named from history, and no revision-bound acceptance evidence exists. Repair route is a repo-owned convention, not an external host change.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Adopt the smallest delivery discipline the repo can own: add a short CONTRIBUTING or README section stating that each commit message names the changed area and intent (for example "admin: rename session column"), and that a commit is not pushed until the documented startup route loads the affected page. Reconcile the convention with the existing project commit conventions before writing. Do not rewrite existing history.

## Validation

- Confirm the convention file exists and matches the project's commit convention memory without contradiction
- Inspect the next commits after adoption and confirm messages name area and intent
expectedOutput: Update the existing Runbook owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.

findings.title: This review window could not tell repeated work from a clean window
findings.reason: Evidence-boundary condition, not a project defect: the admitted Session lane reported zero eligible sessions with source warnings missing-optional-root and disabled-source-root, while the analyzer's separate census read 4 sessions and 73 episode records and reported coverage boundaries Pattern Detection=insufficient-recurrence and Capture/Routing/Application=not-evaluable-missing-normalized-events. Both routes agree that no recurrence decision was constructible this window. Consequence: capability-gap and repeated-work opportunities for this workspace cannot currently be detected or ruled out, and any Learning Capture claim would be unsupported.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Start with bounded discovery, no project mutation: rerun the /better-harness evidence bundle for this workspace over a wider window and compare the Session lane session population with the analyzer census. If the lane still reports zero eligible sessions while sessions exist, record the source-root availability result as the named blocker before any future Learning Capture review is treated as conclusive. Do not invent provider configuration that the discovery step did not observe.

## Validation

- Confirm the rerun Session lane admits at least one eligible session, or produces an explicit named source-availability blocker
- Confirm a later Learning Capture review can distinguish repeat versus clean-window using the admitted episodes
expectedOutput: Update the existing Document owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.
